### #229

- [Summary] Level-loading fidelity: `Load_Level` tail modelled but dead; live load delegates terrain/block decode to the emulator dump
- [Verify] Advanced 2026-06-02: native `level_bounds()` now matches ASM `Load_LevelData loc_15A0` for the header height top bits by adding `Number_blank_top_rows` after the base 14-block screen-height calculation, so camera/death/enemy active bounds include the inserted top rows. Regression `load_leveldata_height_flags_extend_level_bounds_loc_15a0` failed at 448px before the patch and now expects 544px for `height_screens=2,height_flag_bits=3`. Still open: level-loading fidelity audit 2026-05-30 (`docs/source-port/audits/level-loading-fidelity-audit.md`, same workflow) found 18 units, 55 gaps (18 high, 19 medium, 18 low). Most of `Load_Level`'s tail (palette/art/background/scroll/music) is modelled helper-for-helper but dead; the live loader `reload_block_grid_for_level` (`level.rs:17537`) loads only the collision grid + block list + murder wall + weather. **Architectural:** terrain + block-layout decode are delegated to the jgenesis emulator RAM dump (`inspect.rs:1023`), not implemented natively — `Decompress_Chunk`, `AddrTbl_BlockTypes` block-type dispatch, `LoadBlockLayout`, and the theme-collision index have no live native representation (terrain is faithful only for pre-dumped levels). Genuine bug split to child #235 (non-oracle terrain fallback corruption). Evidence: ASM-vs-native, adversarially verified. Gate: per-unit regression + new load scenario + `mise run verify-slice-fast`. DECODER SPIKE 2026-06-03 (Step 0 done): `dump-level-layout` now also dumps `Level_terrain_layout` ($FF52C2) to `<id>.terrain.bin`. Comparing live terrain vs the bundle decoded `foreground.bin` for L01 (160×42) CRACKS the layout mystery that caused prior reconstruction to mismatch 81.8%: bundle `foreground.bin` = 6720 B = 160×42 ROW-MAJOR FG **tile-render** indices (0x0d,0x0e,…); live `Level_terrain_layout` = 8400 B = **30 screens × $118 (20×14 cells/screen) SCREEN-MAJOR collision-terrain bytes** — different size/stride/content, so they are NOT interchangeable. CRUCIALLY the byte VALUES also differ (terrain[0]=0x1b,0x2d,0x1d,0x2e…; fg[0]=0x0d,0x0e,0x0b,0x0c,0x11…), not just the stride — so the bundle `foreground.bin` is a RENDER-oriented tile-index layout, while `Level_terrain_layout` holds the raw FG/skin bytes that `loc_11C34` feeds through `ThemeCollision[byte]` to build `Level_Layout` (low byte = skin = the terrain byte; high nibble = collision). `Level_Layout` ($FFFFA652, $41A0 = 8400 cells × 2) working fixtures read correctly as width×height row-major. So the bundle's decoded fg is NOT the decoder input; the decoder needs the RAW FG resource decompressed into the $118 screen-major terrain byte buffer. FURTHER (Step 1 done): `<id>.terrain.bin` (1b,2d,1d,2e…) matches NONE of the bundle's decoded layers — `foreground.bin`(0d0e render tiles), `block.bin`(442 B object list), `background.bin`(50 B scroll). So `Level_terrain_layout` is GENERATED AT RUNTIME by `Load_Level` (decompress FG resource into the $118 screen-major skin buffer); it is not a reshaped/remapped bundle asset. CONCLUSION: the native decoder must port the ROM terrain generation (`Decompress_Chunk` of the FG resource into the $118=20×14-per-screen buffer) — there is no shortcut via existing bundle files. EXACT ASM (kid.asm:23792-23829): header `(a0)+` = "tile layout address"; `move.w (a0)+,d0; lea (a0,d0.w),a1` splits a control-pointer (a0) and data-pointer (a1); `loc_11C10: bsr Decompress_Chunk` loops into `Level_terrain_layout`; then `loc_11C34/11C36` writes `Level_Layout` cell = `[ThemeCollision_Index[theme][byte]<<4, byte]` per cell across width×height (NOTE: this loop is WIDTH×HEIGHT row-major, confirming Level_Layout is row-major even though the terrain buffer is allocated $118-strided). OPEN PUZZLE to resolve before the port: `decode_saxman(level/foreground/<id>.bin)` (the bundle path, no remap — lib.rs:4091) yields `0d0e…`, but the ROM's `Decompress_Chunk` of the tile-layout resource yields `1b2d…`. The recon equated Decompress_Chunk with Saxman, so either (a) Decompress_Chunk (kid.asm:26143) is NOT the same algorithm as `decode_saxman`, or (b) the bundle's `foreground` resource pointer ≠ the ROM header's tile-layout pointer. PUZZLE RESOLVED 2026-06-03: diffed `Decompress_Chunk` (kid.asm:26143-26210) vs `decode_saxman` (lib.rs:4231) — SAME algorithm (literal / `00` short-ref / `01` long-ref with `$7FF` 11-bit distance = 3 high bits + 1 data byte; same bit-state resume). So the decompressor is already ported as `decode_saxman`. Therefore the bundle's `level/foreground/<id>.bin` is NOT the tile-layout resource `loc_11BEC` decompresses (it must be a different header pointer / a render-graphics layer), since same-algorithm+same-resource would give identical bytes but they differ (0d0e vs 1b2d). DECODER PORT (now small, no new decompressor needed): (1) extract/locate the correct "tile layout" resource — the FIRST long after flag pos in the level header (formats.txt order: FG-tile-layout, block, bg, enemy) — whichever decode_saxmans to the 1b2d skin terrain; (2) `decode_saxman` it; (3) run the already-ported row-major collision map `level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` with `ThemeCollision_Index[theme]` (theme/collision/<theme>.bin) to build Level_Layout low=skin/high=collision; (4) block overlay loc_11C7E; (5) verify byte-equal to `<id>.bin` fixtures across all fixtured levels; (6) wire into `load_block_grid_for_level` for the 4 unreachable bonus levels. The header field/resource identification is the only remaining unknown. UPDATE 2026-06-03: actually the bundle DID split the FG tile-layout pointer into `level/foreground/<id>.bin` (2948 B compressed for L01), so it IS the resource `loc_11BEC` decompresses. Yet `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)`=0d0e while ROM `Decompress_Chunk` of the same →1b2d. Same input+same-algorithm can't differ, so the contradiction means either `decode_saxman` ≠ `Decompress_Chunk` (note: Decompress_Chunk is CHUNKED/RESUMABLE — called in a loop `loc_11C10` with d2 selecting a bit-position resume entry Decompress_BitPos0..6, and writes screen-major to the $118 buffer; `decode_saxman` is a single contiguous pass) OR `foreground.bin` is not literally `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)`. EXACT NEXT EXPERIMENT (Rust harness, ~20 lines): `assert decode_saxman(read("level/foreground/01.bin")) == read("decoded/level/01/foreground.bin")` (confirm the export identity), then compare that decoded output against `01.terrain.bin` (the new dump) cell-for-cell modulo the $118 screen-major stride. If they match → decoder is just decode_saxman + stride-reshape + loc_11C34 (trivial). If they differ → port Decompress_Chunk's chunked/resumable variant. This single test resolves the decoder approach. EXPERIMENT RUN 2026-06-03 (throwaway kid-data example, since removed): `decode_saxman(level/foreground/01.bin)` == `decoded/level/01/foreground.bin` EXACTLY (0d0e…, 6720 B) — confirms the export identity. And that decoded output ≠ `01.terrain.bin` (1b2d…, 8400 B). So the terrain skin layer is NOT decode_saxman of the bundle's foreground resource. foreground/01.bin (2948 B) is the only raw resource large enough to decompress to 6720 cells, yet it yields render tiles (0d0e), not skins. CONCLUSION: either the ROM builds Level_terrain_layout from a resource/pointer the bundle does not currently extract (read the full ROM level header to enumerate ALL layout pointers — header/01.bin is only 12 B, so the bundle stores a reduced header; the 4 layout longs are resolved during extraction), or Decompress_Chunk genuinely differs from decode_saxman on this resource. RESOLVED 2026-06-03: `mapheader_definitions.asm` shows L01 = `maphdr "header/01.bin", ForegroundLayout_01, BlockLayout_01.bin, BackgroundLayout_01, EnemyLayout_01`. The `header/01.bin` is 12 inline bytes (dims/theme/player+flag pos); the FIRST layout long `loc_11BEC` decompresses is `ForegroundLayout_01` = the bundle's `level/foreground/01.bin`. So the terrain SOURCE is confirmed = `foreground/01.bin` (the SAME resource the bundle saxman-decodes). Since `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)`=0d0e but the ROM `Decompress_Chunk` of it →1b2d terrain, and one resource has one compression, **`Decompress_Chunk` is a genuinely different algorithm from `decode_saxman`** (despite similar surface structure; note its chunked/resumable d2 bit-position entry + screen-major $118 writes). decode_saxman's 0d0e is a red herring for terrain (whatever `foreground_layout` uses it for at scene.rs:3047 is a separate concern). COMPLETE DECODER PLAN: port `Decompress_Chunk` (kid.asm:26143-26874) in Rust; run it on `foreground/<id>.bin`; assert output == `<id>.terrain.bin` (the new dump) for all fixtured levels; then row-major `loc_11C34` collision map (`level_layout_cells_loc_11C34`, ported) with `theme/collision/<theme>.bin` + block overlay `loc_11C7E` → assert byte-equal to `<id>.bin` Level_Layout fixtures; finally wire into `load_block_grid_for_level` so the 4 unreachable bonus levels (logical 5A/5D/5E/63) get correct terrain (closes #246 + the bonus half of #238). Everything except the `Decompress_Chunk` port itself is already in place + verifiable against the dumped fixtures. ★ BREAKTHROUGH 2026-06-03 (CORRECTS the above): NO Decompress_Chunk port is needed. The earlier "Decompress_Chunk ≠ decode_saxman / terrain=1b2d" finding was a LOGICAL-vs-RESOURCE ID MIXUP: `dump-level-layout --level 01` warps to LOGICAL 01 = `map_order[1]` = resource 0x4B, but `foreground/01.bin` is RESOURCE 0x01. `map_order[4]`=0x01, so dumping LOGICAL 4 gives resource-0x01 terrain. VERIFIED: `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)` (6720 B) == `dump-level-layout --level 04 → 04.terrain.bin[0..6720]` BYTE-IDENTICAL (`0d0e 0b0c 1112 1314 cf34 0095 9697 9895…`; terrain tail is zero-pad to $20D0). So `Level_terrain_layout = decode_saxman(FG resource)` packed row-major (the $118 "screens" is just the buffer allocation; real data is width×height then zero-padded). FINAL DECODER (wiring, not porting): for a logical level, `r = resource_level_id(level)`; `terrain = decode_saxman(read(foreground/<r>.bin))`; theme from header; `Level_Layout cell = [ThemeCollision[theme][terrain_byte]<<4, terrain_byte]` via the ported `level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` (theme/collision/<theme>.bin); then block overlay `loc_11C7E` from BlockLayout_<r>. Verify byte-equal to `<logical>.bin` fixtures, then wire `load_block_grid_for_level` for the 4 bonus levels. decode_saxman + collision map are BOTH already implemented — the port is small. ★ LANDED 2026-06-03: `decode_level_layout` (level.rs:17753) implements decode_saxman(foreground)→`level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` collision map→BlockGrid, wired as the fixture-absent fallback in `load_block_grid_for_level`. Tests `decode_level_layout_matches_fixture_collision_cells_loc_11c34` (byte-equal plain collision cells, 84/96 levels, 396,871 cells; 12 skipped = the #235 skin/dim-aliased set), `decode_level_layout_gives_unreachable_bonus_levels_a_floor`, `load_block_grid_for_level_falls_back_to_native_decoder` — all pass; gate green (5538+8), clippy clean. REMAINING for full #229 closure: port the block-overlay pass `loc_11C7E` + `sub_127A8` (the `$E0xx` base cells + `$20`/flag overlays) so decoder-only levels also get block-placed collision (currently TODO(fidelity); floors/walls are exact so falling-deaths are fixed). ★ DECOMPRESSOR LANDED 2026-06-03 (CORRECTS earlier "absent from disassembly" claims): `LoadBlockLayout` is NOT absent — it IS at kid.asm:25557 (`loc_132A6`), bit-reader helpers `sub_13618`/`sub_13622`/`sub_1363C`/`sub_1364C`/`loc_13650` at kid.asm:26062-26121 (prior grep missed them because kid.asm has embedded binary — use `rg -a`/`sed`). The "block resource is NOT the same Saxman format" note is correct, but the conclusion "decompressor body absent / cannot port without guessing" was wrong: LoadBlockLayout is a DISTINCT format that REUSES the EniDec MSB-first bit reader (already ported as `EnigmaBitReader`). Ported as `kid_data::decode_block_layout` (lib.rs, after decode_enigma): header = 8 discarded bits + 4-bit X-width (sentinel `(1<<X)-1`) + 4-bit Y-width; main loop `loc_132D6` reads 1 flag bit (ror→bit15) + 5-bit type (`$1F`=terminator), dispatches via `off_132FC` to 11 per-type entry decoders (loc_1331E/1334C/133A0/133DE/1342E/1345E/1347C). Resources need 8 trailing zero pad bytes (ROM reader pre-fetches past the sliced resource end — same margin decode_enigma uses). VERIFIED: all 103 block resources decode to clean `$FFFF`-terminated streams; cross-validating each stream through a throwaway `loc_11C7E` overlay vs the live `Level_Layout` fixtures collapsed the per-level diff from the 6.4% no-overlay baseline to only the cells of the few still-unported overlay handlers — proving the decompressor OUTPUT is correct, not merely well-formed. Tests: `block_layout_05_decodes_to_expected_word_stream_loc_132a6` (golden stream for smallest real resource, kid-data) + `loc_132a6_decodes_block_layout_words_into_the_ffff_terminated_stream` (kid-core wrapper; the old wrongly-Enigma test was replaced). FIX DIRECTION: match the oracle's per-frame camera-follow through the warp-settle window (compare camera_x frame-by-frame from the bootstrap to frame 0) so the settled warp lands on the oracle's tracked camera, not the floored bootstrap. So making `verify-tas` ignore camera at frame 0 would HIDE real divergences when the oracle is reliable — wrong fix. ### #241

- [Verify] NEEDS HUMAN REPRO 2026-06-03. ASM cross-check (recon): native lives logic is faithful and NOT the bug — `apply_damage` (combat.rs:8879) only touches `number_hitpoints`; the HUD lives counter (hud.rs:346) reads `number_lives` only; ASM damage `loc_B700` (kid.asm:14638) never writes `Number_Lives` ($FFFFFC3E), which falls only in `lose_life` (kid.asm:14766) on a true death. `4` is the extra-hitpoint-slot cap, not a lives cap. Most likely the player read the HP PIP row (which DOES drop on a hit) as the lives counter, or this is the #212/#234 HP region. To unblock: capture a `play-native` recording of the hit and identify which top HUD digit changes (top-left lives vs HP pips). No engine change warranted on current evidence. VISUAL EVIDENCE 2026-06-04 (new `capture-scenario-frames` tool on `issue-160-audio-current-enemy-contact`): rendered the HUD at frames 285 (pre-hit) and 295 (post-hit) across the dragon contact. The LIVES counter (top-right `Nx` with the kid-head icon) stays at `3x` BEFORE and AFTER the hit — confirming the live lives logic does not decrement on contact, matching the ASM. The HP indicator is the two circle pips TOP-LEFT (base Kid = 2). So the playtest "6 lives → 4 on a hit" is the TOP-LEFT HP pip count (a helmet gives more pips; a hit knocks the helmet off and drops the pips instantly — correct KC behaviour), read as the lives counter. The "helmet fell on floor and didn't pick up" is also correct: a knocked-off helmet is lost, not re-collectable. STRONG EVIDENCE this is a HUD-reading confusion, not a lives bug — but still needs a human to confirm against a HELMET+hit capture (this recording is base Kid). Recommend [-] (not a bug) on human confirmation.

### #245

- [Summary] 2026-06-03 playtest: dying can leave the screen black/frozen (looks stuck)
- [Verify] FIXED 2026-06-04: root cause was a one-frame-late death-arc launch introduced by commit `0108599e` (Defer player contact damage to next object pass). That commit deferred ALL player contact damage by one frame to fix the #211 walk route, but the death-causing landing-dragon graze already had a one-frame landing-defer guard (`2572ebf2`), so the deferral double-delayed it: death landed on frame 1685 instead of the oracle's 1684, shifting the entire death→tumble→lose_life→respawn sequence one frame. Follow-up commit `40b205e9` then bumped `PLAYER_DEATH_HIDE_FRAMES` 32→40 (+SHELL/CAMERA) to compensate, over-shifting the hidden window by ~8 frames and drifting the visible respawn bootstrap from oracle frame 1791 to ~1799. The death-respawn cache-backed regression tests were left red on main with values matching neither native nor oracle. Fix: apply the grounded dragon-graze contact in-frame (combat.rs ~10558) instead of queueing it, so the death lands on oracle frame 1684; restore `PLAYER_DEATH_HIDE_FRAMES=32` (keeping the loc_b8de Level-2 `HIDE-SHELL`/`HIDE-CAMERA` relationships). Verified against oracle window `death_respawn_level1_window_01700_01855_step_1`: tumble arc, lose_life (f1759), bootstrap pose (f1791 `(0x160,0x44)`), and slide-to-hold (f1855 `(0x40,0x68)`) all byte-match. All 7 previously-failing `death_respawn_level_1_*` cache-backed tests now pass (cache-backed kid-core failures 73→66, the remaining 66 are unrelated published_tas/demo/snapshot/IntroSequence/prize-cell). Known residual: the invisible hidden-pose/camera `None`-clear is one frame early on Level 1 because the hide window is a single global constant that Level 1 (`HIDE-SHELL=11`) and the Level 2 loc_b8de probe (`HIDE-SHELL=13`) genuinely disagree on — a per-route oracle-derived hide window is the proper follow-up (does not affect the visible respawn). Min gate: 1p-playable. REJECTED-APPROACH 2026-06-04: an oracle probe found a SEPARATE minor residual — on a STEADY walk into the Level-0 walking dragon (kid_y_velocity==0 throughout, no landing frame) native applies the contact graze ONE FRAME EARLY (number_hitpoints drops at frame 60 vs oracle frame 61). Cause: the grounded DragonWalking graze consumes in-frame (correct for THIS #245 landing case, where the falling frame absorbs the defer), but a steady-grounded walk-in has no landing frame so it should defer one frame via the shared pending_player_contact_damage queue. Routing the grounded graze UNIFORMLY through the pending queue FIXES the steady-walk case but REGRESSES #245 (verified: 7 death_respawn_level_1_* tests fail — re-introduces the double-delay, death at 1685 not 1684). So the correct fix must DISTINGUISH landing (airborne->ground this frame -> in-frame consume) from steady-grounded (defer); a uniform approach cannot satisfy both. Deferred — minor 1-frame damage-timing on the L0 dragon steady-walk only; #245's visible death-respawn is correct.

### #247

- [Summary] Theme collision table trimmed: high skin indices lose their real ROM collision nibble (was misattributed to the closed #235)
- [Verify] FIXED 2026-06-03: the bundle slices each `theme/collision/<name>.bin` at the NEXT pointer (`.cache/upstream/kid-chameleon-disasm/tools/to_split.txt:15-25`), so e.g. `swamp.bin` is 252 B (own length). But ASM loc_11C36 (`kid.asm:23818`) indexes `ThemeCollision_Index[theme]` with the FULL 8-bit skin byte (`move.b (a0,d2.w),d3`) and the tables are packed contiguously (`unk_7BB64`..`unk_7C4EC`, `kid.asm:46114`), so a high skin deliberately reads into the FOLLOWING theme — the ROM has no per-theme length check. The decoder previously zero-padded the trimmed slice to 256 (= passable), losing those nibbles: swamp skin 254 reads $06/Solid from the adjacent `mountain` table in the ROM but decoded as Empty. Fix: new `theme_collision_table_loc_11C36` (`crates/kid-core/src/level.rs`) reconstructs the contiguous region by concatenating the sibling files in pointer order (verified byte-identical to `kid.bin[0x7BB64..0x7C4EC]`) and returns the 256 bytes from this theme's base, so high skins read the adjacent theme exactly as the ROM does. Wired into `decode_level_layout`, removing the zero-pad. RESULT: the genuine collision-table residual on the #229 decoder oracle drops to ZERO — `decode_level_layout_matches_fixture_collision_cells_loc_11c34` goes from byte-exact 418384/74-of-83 to 418385/75-of-83 cells/levels, and the only remaining residual is the runtime-toggled overlay class (L0x3F island, in-range skins the `loc_11C7E` overlay pass cleared because the idle dump captured a toggleable block mid-animation — NOT a table defect; verified the table lookup is correct there). The earlier #229/#235 evidence that lumped L0x3F skins 202/207/237 into "collision-table extraction defects" was wrong: those skins are in-range (island own length 252) and the table returns $06 correctly; the divergence is the overlay class. New regression `theme_collision_table_reads_into_adjacent_theme_loc_11c36` pins swamp[254]=$06. Bundle `.bin` files unchanged (the data was already correct; only the read was trimmed). / The #229 decoder residual is now reduced to the runtime-animation overlay class only. ASM-vs-native, adversarially verified against the live `Level_Layout` fixtures. Gate: `theme_collision_table_reads_into_adjacent_theme_loc_11c36` + the rewritten full-byte-equality decoder oracle (`KID_ENABLE_CACHE_BACKED_TESTS=1`) + standard lib/clippy.

### #248

- [Summary] 2026-06-04 playtest: death → black/frozen screen for NON-dragon-graze deaths (well-fall, spikes, jump-into-wall, out-of-continues), inputs dead, music continues
- [Verify] #245 fixed the Level-1 grounded-dragon-graze death-respawn TIMING (byte-matches oracle), but the player reports the black/frozen-on-death symptom STILL occurs in live play for other death triggers: falling down the Level-2 well, jumping into a wall, hitting spikes, and especially when out of continues. Repeatedly: "Death sequence... black and nothing else happening. Sound playing. Press start/A/B nothing" — i.e. the death state machine reaches a hung state with no tumble/respawn and dead input. Likely a DIFFERENT death path than #245's dragon-graze: candidates are (a) the falling-off/pit death (`Death` via `sub_902A` loc_9142 / level_height bound), (b) the spike/hazard death, (c) the game-over/no-continues flow (ASM lose_life → game over when Number_Lives exhausted). NEEDS: reproduce a non-dragon death (pit-fall or spike) in a DynamicScenario, capture native trace through death, compare game_mode/lifecycle/respawn against oracle; check the game-over branch when lives==0. Min gate: 1p-playable death→respawn on pit/spike, and a sane game-over screen with live input. ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-06-04 (reproduced + diagnosed): rendered `issue-160-audio-current-enemy-contact` (death at ~frame 431) via the new `capture-scenario-frames` — frames 445/480/560 (and presumably to the 600-frame end) are ALL FULLY BLACK. The cause is the death→respawn lifecycle: after the death tumble, native enters `PlayerLifecycle::Respawning { remaining_frames: PLAYER_DEATH_RESPAWN_SETTLE_FRAMES }` with `PLAYER_DEATH_RESPAWN_SETTLE_FRAMES = 7_210` (constants.rs:396) — a ~2-MINUTE hidden mode-8 bootstrap hold. During Dying/Respawning the game-mode maps to `GameMode::LevelTransition` (native_player/mod.rs:6057), which the player renders BLACK. The 7210 value was deliberately tuned to match an IDLE oracle STATE trace ("death-respawn-level1 window compare still reports the mode-8 bootstrap hold pose through frame 9000"), and the constant comment explicitly admits "the later visible `Load_InGame` return is still a separate frontier" — i.e. the VISIBLE level-return after the mode-8 bootstrap is UNIMPLEMENTED. So #245's state tests pass (they compare the hidden-bootstrap trace, not pixels) while live play shows black for ~2 min and never visibly respawns. This is NOT primarily the game-over/no-continues branch (that lifecycle path exists in boot.rs:7576/7613); it is the normal death→respawn visible-return gap, which also makes every death look hung. EXACT FIX PATH: implement the visible `Load_InGame` respawn return — after the mode-8 bootstrap hold, transition game-mode back to `InGame` with the grounded respawn pose and re-render the level, on a timeline matching the oracle's visible respawn (NOT the 7210-frame idle-trace hold). Must keep the #245 `death_respawn_level1_window_*` STATE window green (those compare the hidden bootstrap), so the visible-return likely needs its own shorter live timeline distinct from the long settle-state used for the oracle STATE compare. Reproduce with `capture-scenario-frames` before/after to confirm the level re-appears within ~1-2s of death. MECHANISM CONFIRMED 2026-06-04 (trace.rs:6787 `game_mode()`): `Dying` / `Respawning` BOTH map to `GameMode::LevelTransition` for the whole 7210-frame hold, and `Respawning` is a fixed countdown (boot.rs:7629) that IGNORES input — which is exactly why the player's "press start/A/B → nothing" does nothing during the black hold. The death respawn does NOT go through the `StartingLevel` title-card path that accepts a Start edge (#238); it sits in the input-dead `Respawning` countdown. BLOCKER FOR THE FIX: the #245 `death_respawn_level1_window_*` tests compare native game_mode/pose against an oracle trace that stays in mode-8 "through frame 9000" — i.e. an IDLE death-respawn with no input to advance. A real death-respawn auto-returns to the VISIBLE level in ~2-3s, so the idle-trace 7210 hold and a quick live respawn cannot both come from one constant. PREREQUISITE before coding: capture a NEW oracle trace of a PROGRESSING death-respawn (one that actually reaches visible `Load_InGame`/`Game_Mode=$0C` gameplay again) and derive the real visible-return timeline from it; then drive the live respawn off that (game-mode back to InGame + grounded pose) while keeping the idle-state window for the existing STATE compare. Do NOT shorten 7210 blindly — it will redden the #245 state window. This is the single highest-impact playability fix; it is a focused next pass gated on the new progressing-respawn oracle capture. ASM CONFIRMS DIRECTION 2026-06-04 (`lose_life` → `move.w #8,(Game_Mode)` → `jmp (j_loc_6E2)`; `loc_6E2` kid.asm:823): the real death-respawn re-enters the SAME path as a level load — `loc_6E2` clears all VRAM, re-inits object/gfx slots, calls `LoadGameModeData`, then runs `MainGameLoop`/`Mode_Level`. So a real respawn is a QUICK VRAM-clear → level reload → playable (~1s of reload-black, then the level returns and Kid is controllable), NOT a 7210-frame black hold. The render path is `build_scene_filtered` (scene.rs:738): `GameMode::LevelTransition` → `build_transition_scene` (scene.rs:753) which paints the whole frame BLACK + title-card glyphs; a death-respawn has no title-card workers so it is PURE black. FIX = make the death-respawn reload the level and return to `InGame` (visible + input-live) on the real ~1s timeline. REMAINING BLOCKER (unchanged): the #245 `death_respawn_level1_window_*` STATE tests compare against an IDLE oracle trace that stays mode-8 to ~frame 9000 (no input advances it), so a quick live return would mismatch that idle window. The fix needs a fresh INTERACTIVE respawn oracle capture (give input after death, observe when the oracle returns control / game_mode→$0C) to set the live timeline, then keep the idle-state settle only for the STATE compare. Direction is certain; the timeline number must come from the interactive oracle capture, not a guess. PRIMARY FIX LANDED 2026-06-04 (Respawning now accepts a Start edge to resume): the `Respawning` arm (boot.rs `step_lifecycle`) resumes to `Alive` on a Start rising edge (`input.start && !previous_input.start`), mirroring the #238 StartingLevel Game_Mode=8 hand-off, so the player's "press start -> nothing / stuck on black" is FIXED: Start resumes, game_mode()->InGame, and the level re-renders with Kid grounded. Verified 5 ways: new tests `respawn_hold_resumes_on_start_edge_loc_6e2` + `respawn_hold_without_start_keeps_counting_down_for_state_parity`; all 30 #245 `death_respawn` cache-backed STATE tests still pass (they never press Start, so the idle window is untouched); verify-slice-fast green (5549); clippy clean; and VISUAL via `capture-scenario-frames` on a Start-pressing death scenario (frame 555 black hold, 575/595 level restored with lives decremented). Marked [?] pending human playtest. REGRESSION 2026-06-06: `spike_death_triggers_death_and_respawn` now drives the real spike hazard path into `Respawning`, presses Start, and asserts `PlayerLifecycle::Alive`, `GameMode::InGame`, `BootState::InGame`, lives decremented once, and a live Kid pose. This extends the earlier synthetic `Respawning` Start-edge test to a concrete non-dragon death trigger from the playtest report. Verified with `cargo test -q -p kid-core spike_death -- --nocapture`, `cargo test -q -p kid-core respawn_hold -- --nocapture`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `hk run pre-commit`. REGRESSION 2026-06-06: `continue_restores_lives_and_respawns` now follows the real out-of-lives path through `GameOver` → `ContinueCountdown` → `Respawning`, releases the continue-button frame, presses Start again, and asserts `Alive`, `GameMode::InGame`, `BootState::InGame`, and a live Kid pose. RESIDUAL FOLLOW-UPS (need the interactive-respawn oracle capture): (1) before Start the hold renders black, not the level title card the original shows during Game_Mode=8; (2) the no-input auto-timeout is still the 7210 idle-trace value, not the real short auto-resume - derive it from the interactive oracle capture and shorten it while keeping the #245 idle-state window green.

### #249

- [Verify] In the Level-2 well, hitting the LEFT wall makes Kid "jump straight up to the top" with no C/jump input; also observed with a helmet form. Previously noted in the 2026-06-03 playtest as "wall-grab zoom-to-top teleport (Samurai/Rhino)". The wall-cling/grab live path is firing an upward launch unconditionally on wall contact instead of requiring the ASM climb input. So for BASE Kid the "fly to top without C" can only happen if `jump_buffer_frames` is spuriously non-zero on wall contact (investigate the jump-buffer set/clear around wall-sticky), OR the well geometry defeats the head-clearance gates so it pulls up cell-by-cell to the shaft top. The HELMET case ("had the other guy's helmet on") is a DIFFERENT mechanism — helmet forms are excluded from this pull-up (returns false at form check), so the helmet "fly up" is a climbing-form path (IronKnight/Skycutter/Cyclone vertical) firing on wall contact. SPLIT #249 into base-Kid (jump-buffer/head-gate) and helmet (climb-form) when reproducing. Reproduction prerequisite: a Level-2 well scenario per form (use `playtest_form` + `capture-scenario-frames` to see the launch), since the mechanism is form-dependent and not safely fixable without seeing which path fires. ### #250

- [Summary] 2026-06-04 playtest: growing/evanescent blocks and spike-shooter blocks confused — growing blocks emit spikes and get destroyed by the spikes
- [Verify] Player hypothesis (Level 4, the hit-to-grow block area): "the blocks have got confused between the growing ones and the spike-shooting ones" — growing blocks appear to shoot spikes, and the spikes then destroy the blocks. Suggests the block-class dispatch is wrongly mapping evanescent/grow blocks (`loc_1117A`/`loc_11188` evanescent reveal in weather.rs) to the shooter-block class (`F25C`/`F2EE` shooter, #065/#214). Cross-ref #214 (Highwater shooter live path) and #242 (rubber/bouncy block id confusion). NEEDS: Level-4 recording around the grow-block stack; check block skin→class resolution and projectile spawn source. Min gate: grow blocks grow and are not destroyed by spurious self-spikes. ASM INVESTIGATION 2026-06-04 (found a real lead AND a contradiction to resolve): the shooter SCAN `shooter_direction_bits_loc_F106` (blocks.rs:506) has TWO branches — (1) ASM-correct: `BlockType::Drill`(nibble $C) && skin>=$2D → skin-$2D, matching ASM `loc_F106` which does `andi.w #$F00,d6; cmpi.w #$C00,d6` (ONLY nibble $C fires; real Highwater shooters are `$EC2F` = nibble C); (2) an ADDED branch firing `BlockType::Shooter`(8) / `BlockType::Mushroom`(9). Per the block-type taxonomy (terrain.rs: Shooter=8, Mushroom=9, Evanescent=$A, Drill=$C) and the ASM hit-interaction table `off_BB80[9] -> loc_BBC2 -> loc_11430`, type-9 blocks run `sub_114C0`/`sub_114F4` (kid.asm:23434) which WRITE block-layout tiles (`$EF1B`/`$EF1A`/`$E919`) via `sub_11530` into the FG update queue and `EraseBlockFromLevelLayout` — i.e. a block ANIMATION/regrow worker, NOT a projectile shooter. So strictly per `loc_F106`, type-9 (`$E919`, nibble 9) should NOT fire (andi `$F00` of `$E919` = `$900` != `$C00`). THIS matches the player's "grow blocks shoot spikes" bug. CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE BEFORE CHANGING: existing tests `runtime_tests.rs:8688-8756` deliberately make `$E919` type-9 blocks FIRE, citing ASM `loc_11430`/`sub_114F4` and "the first Highwater Pass 2 `$E919` touch block fires after its support worker wakes" — apparently oracle-derived. So either (a) Highwater `$E919` blocks DO fire (the branch is right there) and only LEVEL-4 grow blocks are wrongly caught (then the fix is a skin/level distinction, but engine-level not per-level), or (b) the prior tests encode a misread and `$E919` should never fire. RESOLUTION REQUIRED (do not guess — sources disagree): reproduce BOTH against the oracle — a Highwater Pass 2 `$E919` block (does it fire spikes in the real game?) AND a Level-4 grow block (does it fire?), via `capture-scenario-frames` + oracle. If Highwater fires but Level-4 doesn't, find the ASM discriminator (skin range within nibble-9, or a different block type for Level-4 grow). Did NOT change code: removing the Shooter / Mushroom branch would break the oracle-cited Highwater shooter tests and may be wrong. REFINEMENT 2026-06-04: read those two tests (`level3_type9_mushroom_block_uses_shooter_slot_path_after_touch`, `highwater_pass_2_first_e919_touch_block_spawns_shooter_projectiles`, runtime_tests.rs:8685/8723) — they are SYNTHETIC and CIRCULAR: each hand-builds a single `$E919` cell in a vec grid and asserts native spawns projectiles, i.e. they assert exactly what the added Mushroom branch produces. They cite ASM but are NOT emulator/oracle comparisons, so they are NOT ground truth that the real game fires `$E919` blocks — they lock in the prior author's interpretation. So neither my `loc_F106` reading (nibble-C only → `$E919` should not fire) NOR these tests are oracle-confirmed. DECISIVE RESOLUTION (still required, now clearly the only way): run a Highwater Pass 2 `$E919` "touch-then-shoot" block AND a Level-4 grow block through the EMULATOR/oracle (`compare-native-oracle` / `verify-tas` on a real route, not a synthetic vec grid) and observe whether each actually spawns a projectile in the real game. Frames 1..359 are score-clean, so the +40 is awarded in a single event at frame 360, but the enemy roster is EMPTY on both sides at that checkpoint (no visible enemy/block death), so the source is a non-roster score award (prize, EOL/flag bonus, or a delayed kill credit). This is the Juggernaut flag-transition recording, so candidates: a Juggernaut-specific kill/score, a flag/EOL bonus timing, or (relating to #250) a grow-block destruction crediting score the oracle does not. NEEDS: tas-diff the full state (not just enemy frontier) at frames 358-360 to find which score-source field/event fires (diamonds, prize, EOL bonus, block destroy), then trace that award path vs ASM. Min gate: Highwater Pass 2 score matches oracle through the flag transition. Possibly the same root as #250 (wrong block/enemy destruction crediting score) — cross-ref. DEEPER 2026-06-04 (full-state `--frontier-kind gameplay` tas-diff at frames 359-360): alongside the score +40, `number_objects` is native=3 vs oracle=20 — native has ~17 FEWER objects than the oracle in Highwater Pass 2. That is far beyond the normal +2/+3 native object-count modelling, so it is a real roster divergence: native is either UNDER-SPAWNING Highwater Pass 2's objects (strongly aligns with #214 "top shooter blocks do not all move/fire" — fewer shooter-block objects) OR native has reached the flag/EOL and cleared objects while the oracle is still mid-level (this is the Juggernaut flag-transition recording). The score +40 is likely downstream of this object divergence. CROSS-REF #214 (Highwater Pass 2 shooter blocks) — the under-spawned objects are probably the missing shooter blocks. NEXT: enumerate the native vs oracle object roster at frame 359 (which 17 objects is native missing?) to confirm they are the Highwater Pass 2 shooter blocks (→ merge with #214) vs a flag/EOL progress desync. This is a real, oracle-found Highwater Pass 2 divergence regardless of which. CAVEAT 2026-06-04: the player PLAYED Highwater Pass 2 and SAW its enemies (Hand, shooters, grow blocks), so native is NOT broadly under-spawning the level — which makes native=3 objects at frame 359 more likely a FLAG/EOL PROGRESS DESYNC specific to this `juggernaut-flag-frontier` PROBE recording (native reached/cleared objects at the flag while the oracle is still mid-level) than a general object-spawn bug. Lower priority and likely recording-specific; do not conflate with the user-facing #214/#250 unless a NON-flag Highwater Pass 2 recording reproduces the object/score gap mid-level. RESOLVED-INTERPRETATION 2026-06-04 (read-only, definitive): at the frame-359 onset `kid_x_pos`, `game_mode`, AND `level_complete` all MATCH native vs oracle (not in the diff), and BOTH enemy rosters are empty — so Kid is at the same place/mode and the 17 extra oracle objects are NON-ENEMY objects. At a Highwater Pass 2 FLAG TRANSITION those are EOL/flag-sequence workers (score-digit/bonus-text/flag objects) that native models as a COLLAPSED EOL sequence rather than spawning each as an object; the score +40 is EOL-bonus award timing. So #253 is native's known collapsed-EOL/flag modelling (fewer objects + EOL bonus on a slightly different frame), the same advisory class as other EOL divergences — LIKELY EXPECTED, not a user-facing gameplay bug. Downgrade to P3/likely-`[-]`: only a real bug if the EOL bonus TOTAL (not just per-frame timing) ends up wrong, or if a non-flag mid-level Pass 2 recording shows the gap. Not the user's grow-block symptom (#250) and not mid-level object loss (#214).

### #284

- [Summary] 2026-06-10 playtest: later-level prize blocks award diamonds instead of their configured helmet contents (intro-demo Cyclops prize gives a diamond; player cannot obtain new helmets at later levels)
- [Verify] Evidence source: human playtest on the 325e8622 build. Cross-ref #274 (the demo-level instance). Suspect the prize-content/blocklist decode for higher resource levels or the floating-item content mapping; verify with `kidcli inspect-level` block lists for the affected levels vs oracle WRAM prize objects. Progression-blocking for forms.
- [Verify] Fixed 2026-06-10 in b0e2a098. Root cause: generated Block List RAM dumps for later levels can place foreground-update queue data immediately after the real `loc_12434`/`loc_12480` prize records. The parser accepted those spill records because it only read byte 7's low nibble, so property word `$0100` became content id `0` (Diamond), duplicating real Cyclone/Eyeclops/Juggernaut layout addresses as diamonds. Native now treats the full prize property word like the ASM: bit 15 is the disguised flag and only the low nibble is content, with middle bits rejecting the record as spill. Regressions: `block_list_from_raw_generated_ram_dump_stops_prizes_before_fg_queue_spill`, cache-backed `generated_later_level_prize_block_list_ignores_fg_queue_spill_diamonds`, and `generated_later_level_juggernaut_prize_survives_live_block_lifecycle`. Coverage is complete: every family has an **exact-value box-edge** `*_contact_uses_rom_collision_size_row_loc_1bce` test (asserts all four edges, e.g. combat_tests.rs:1140 UFO `(-14,14,-27,-3)`), asymmetric families have an exact `*_right_facing_flips_via_loc_1be4` test, and zero/death rows are pinned. So the contact-box vein has no bug and no test gap left. Tooling note: `cargo mutants -f combat.rs --re 'contact_bounds'` does **not** scope this large file — `--re` is ignored by `--list` and the run still tested non-contact functions (`process_stomps`, `apply_pending_enemy_collisions`); do not retry whole-file mutation here. ### #316

- Filed 2026-06-11 umbrella: audits/helmets-fidelity-audit.md, 25 of 38 still open after the staleness check.
- Progress 2026-06-20: fixed the Five-Way Shot projectile lifecycle row. ASM `DiamondPower_Main_FiveWayShot loc_4019A` treats `Diamond_power_timer` as a signed word after it reaches zero: visible slots stay alive at timer zero, then negative multiples of eight decrement each slot's size and `sub_3F5E8` removes them on underflow. Native was clearing slot-owned Five-Way Shot at generic timer zero because `diamond_power_frames` was an unsigned countdown and the live path never reached the negative fade. Runtime now treats Five-Way Shot and Wall of Death as slot-owned fade powers, wraps the timer word through signed negative values while slots remain, and clears only after the slot list self-removes. ### #322

**P0 CRASH — shooting a flying dragon (Under Skull Mountain 3 / Level 0x06) panics `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0`.** Filed 2026-06-18 from a human playtest ("a little dragon that's flying. I jumped up and I shot him and then it crashed"). Investigated by parallel triage workflow + adversarial verify + manual follow-up.

- **Status of root cause: UNPINNED.** The exact panic line could not be determined by static analysis. `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 mise run play-native` on Level 0x06 is required to capture the file:line (needs a display — human action).
- **RULED OUT (do not re-trace):**
  - `crates/kidcli/src/native_player/sprites.rs:1499-1502` unguarded `& enemy_visuals.frames[frame_index]` after `% frames.len()` — the first triage agent proposed this, but adversarial verify REFUTED it: for object_type 0x0C the `frames` Vec is statically length 9 (built one-per-descriptor from the fixed `EnemyFamilySpec.frames` in kid-render/src/bundle.rs ~1538; theme only swaps palette/pixels, `apply_enemy_art_permutation` is in-place + forest-only). `% 9` and the index are always in range.
  - `enemies.rs:15238 script[cmd]` / `enemies.rs:15322 match script[0]` — `dragon_script()` (enemies.rs:8740) always returns one of `DRAGON_SCRIPT_0/1/2` (6/4/5 entries; enemies.rs:8714-8745), never empty. An over-range `cmd` would print "len is 6…", not "len is 0…".
  - `combat.rs:8174/8197/8206 slots[0]/workers[0]` (boss-eye / HeadyMetal scatter) — fixed-size arrays, and gated to Shishkaboss/BoomerangBosses/HeadyMetal, not the flying dragon.
  - `combat.rs:8786 boss_eye_breakup_trigger_words_fb72_fb74_fb76[trigger_index]` — fixed 3-word array, family-gated to bosses.
  - Enemy-family render `frames[0]` (`sprites.rs:1494`, `scene.rs:5602 push_effect_enemy_sprite`) require a present-but-EMPTY family Vec; `load_compressed_sprite_frames` (bundle.rs:4175) returns len == descriptor count and no `EnemyFamilySpec` has empty `frames`, and on decode failure `load_enemy_visuals` `continue`s (never inserts) — so in production no family loads empty.
- **Most likely true home (verifier's lead):** a runtime `[0]`/`[idx]` into a per-object Vec in the kid-core projectile→flying-dragon-death path that genuinely drains to empty at kill time (active enemies / projectiles / death-child / descent-fire lists), OR a render `frames[0]` reached via a child/effect object_type loaded from a path other than `ENEMY_FAMILIES`. The player's form throws the green-dot Maniaxe axe (#323), which sets the dragon HP→0 — the crash fires at the kill/render of that frame.
- **Robust engine-level fix (correct regardless of the exact line):** make the render `frames[0]`/`% len()` sites total against empty frames — guard `frames.is_empty()` and fall back to the existing `object_rect(...)` placeholder (sprites.rs:1518) / early-return (scene.rs:5601), and have `load_enemy_visuals` skip inserting a family whose decoded `frames` is empty so `families.get` returns None and the rect fallback fires. Add a probe scenario that shoots a flying dragon + a unit test that `select_enemy_frame`/`push_enemy_sprite` do not panic for object_type 0x0C with empty/len<5 frames (alive and HP==0+wait_timer). Cite ASM `Dragon_Flying.asm loc_346DA stru_34600` / `loc_3492C stru_345E4`.
- Evidence: combat.rs:8857-8924 (dragon death child/anim, guarded), helmets.rs:5984-6075 (friendly-projectile hit, guarded), enemies.rs:15393 (descent-fire spawn). All these gameplay paths are bounds-checked; the unguarded indexes are the render `frames[0]` and any not-yet-located per-object `[0]`.

**2026-06-18 (latest+18) — `[ ]`→`[b]`, blocked on human repro. Docs-only.** First substantive
investigation since filing. Two findings that change the disposition:

1. **The proposed "robust render-guard fix" is provably DEAD CODE — do NOT implement it (it would be
   churn).** A present-but-empty enemy family cannot occur in production: `load_enemy_visuals`
   (kid-render/src/bundle.rs:3489-3554) inserts a family **only** after `load_compressed_sprite_frames`
   returns `Ok` — on any `Err` it `eprintln!`s and `continue`s (never inserts). `load_compressed_sprite_frames`
   (bundle.rs:4175-4194) returns exactly one `SpriteFrame` per descriptor, so its Vec is empty **iff** the
   spec's `frames` slice is empty — and **no** `ENEMY_FAMILIES` spec has `frames: &[]` (grep over the 34
   specs: zero matches). So `families.get(&type)` is either absent (→ `push_enemy_sprite` already falls back
   to `object_rect`, sprites.rs:1512-1520) or present-with-≥1-frame. The `frames[0]`/`% len()` sites
   (sprites.rs:1494/1502, scene.rs:5602 `push_effect_enemy_sprite` — itself boss-gated to types 0x20/0x21)
   are therefore unreachable on an empty Vec; guarding them changes no observable behaviour. The archive's
   "skip empty-frame family inserts" half is likewise a no-op (no empty spec exists).
2. **The kid-core flying-dragon (0x0C → `EnemyFamily::Dragon`) kill paths are all already bounds-safe.**
   Re-audited the full shoot→HP0→death→child chain: `DRAGON_DIVE_SCRIPT[descent_index]` is preceded by a
   `>= len()` check (enemies.rs:15356-15360); the friendly-projectile-hit loops iterate `0..active_enemies.len()`,
   collect `kill_indices`, and remove in **reverse after** the loop (helmets.rs:5943-5975, 5990-6076) — no
   stale in-loop index; `step_pending_dragon_death_children` / `apply_dragon_flying_death_status_route_loc_3492C`
   / `rebuild_active_enemy_roster` use `retain_mut` + iterators + `get_mut` (combat.rs:8957-9012, 8934-8955).
   The 0x0C death-frame render arm is guarded `len() >= 4` (sprites.rs:1372) and the fallthrough uses `% len()`
   (a divisor-zero panic, *not* "index out of bounds"), so it isn't the reported panic either.

**Conclusion:** there is no safe blind fix, and the exact `[0]`-on-empty-Vec site cannot be pinned by static
analysis (this iteration's audit + the original 15-agent triage both failed to). Pinning genuinely requires
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1 mise run play-native` on Level 0x06 (interactive: enter the Maniaxe/Iron-Knight form, jump,
shoot a flying dragon) — needs a display, which the unattended/headless loop lacks. Blocked on that human run
per the status legend's "needs human repro". Once a human supplies the backtrace file:line, the fix is a
targeted bounds-guard at that one site + a regression scenario — not the speculative render-guard sweep above.

**2026-06-18 (latest+21) — `[b]`→`[?]`, fixed render empty-frame hardening candidate.** Although the exact
human crash file:line remains unpinned, the renderer totality holes from the crash lead are now closed with
red/green coverage:

- `build_scene_falls_back_to_enemy_rect_for_empty_loaded_family_issue322` first failed red on
  `sprites.rs` `% frames.len()` with a divisor-zero panic when object_type 0x0C had a present but empty loaded
  family. `push_enemy_sprite` now checks `enemy_visuals.frames.is_empty()` before calling `select_enemy_frame`
  and falls back to the existing `object_rect` placeholder.
- `build_scene_skips_empty_effect_enemy_family_issue322` covers effect-only enemy art (HeadyMetal split pieces
  through `push_effect_enemy_sprite`); empty loaded frames now early-return instead of indexing `frames[0]`.

This is a robust render hardening fix, not proof of the original live crash root cause. Human validation remains:
replay Under Skull Mountain 3 Level 0x06 and shoot a flying dragon with the axe form. If it still crashes, capture
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1 mise run play-native` and record the file:line for the next targeted fix.

### #323

**Maniaxe / Iron Knight axe renders as a green dot, and "does not hurt enemies".** Two faults, separated.

- **Fault 1 — green dots (REAL, never implemented, NOT a regression).** `active_projectile_kind()` (kid-core/src/trace.rs:78-156) tags ~25 projectile kinds but has **no `ManiaxeAxe` arm**, so the axe (`EnemyProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe`, types.rs:2975) falls through to `ActiveProjectileKind::Generic` (trace.rs:154). `ActiveProjectileKind` (types.rs:75-143) has **no `ManiaxeAxe` variant** at all (`git log -S'ActiveProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe'` over crates/ returns nothing — never existed). play-native draws a `Generic` friendly projectile as a 4×4 rect in `FRIENDLY_PROJECTILE_COLOUR = [100,255,100]` (scene.rs:7) via the `Generic | LionProjectile` arm (scene.rs:4467-4480) = the green dot. Real art `ingame/artunc_kid/maniaxe_axe_1..4.bin` (disasm tools/to_split.txt:289-292) is unwired in kid-render.
- **Fault 2 — does not hurt (NOT reproduced at engine level; NOT a #296 regression).** `process_friendly_projectile_hits` (helmets.rs:5984-6028) keeps the lifetime-0 axe alive (helmets.rs:5992) and delivers `take_colid_hurt_or_queue_death` (helmets.rs:6014) with the ROM `unk_318B2` axe box; axe spawns `friendly:true kind:ManiaxeAxe lifetime:0` (helmets.rs:6591-6604). `cargo test -p kid-core maniaxe_axe` → 25 pass incl the #296 regression `live_maniaxe_axe_lifetime_zero_damages_and_deletes_loc_8abc`. Most plausibly the human could not see the tiny green dot land; if it still fails to hurt with the correct sprite, that's a SEPARATE play-native repro.
- **Fix:** add `ActiveProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe` + the trace.rs arm; wire `maniaxe_axe_1..4.bin` into kid-render and a scene.rs draw arm (mirror the boss/shooter sprite arms). Dead ends ruled out: not a collision regression (#296 intact), not a missing `friendly` flag, not the fire-demon signature heuristic — it is the plain `Generic` default.
- **Investigation 2026-06-18 (latest+19, stays `[ ]` — no code, not a quick verified fix).** Pinned the ROM sprite source: `ManiaxeAxe_Init` (kid.asm:9833) installs animation `stru_8B86` (kid.asm:9995-9999) which cycles **4** frames `LnkTo_unk_A589E/A5924/A59AA/A5A30` (the per-frame mapping headers, 6 bytes before each `maniaxe_axe_N.bin` art start per to_split.txt:289-292; the Maniaxe mappings block begins at ROM 0x0A589E per `doc/Kid Chameleon hacking.txt:174`). The axe is a Kid-form projectile, so its frames belong on the **Maniaxe `PlayerFormVisuals`** (form keyed by `current_helmet_id`), not the enemy-family table that the existing sprite arms (tank/robot) pull from. **Wiring plan (4 files):** (1) add `pub axe: Vec<SpriteFrame>` to `PlayerFormVisuals` (player.rs) + `axe: &'static [PlayerFrameDescriptor]` to `PlayerFormSpec` (bundle.rs:1115, default `&[]` for the 8 non-Maniaxe specs + the fallback at bundle.rs:3811 + any test-fixture literals) and `axe: load_player_frames(manifest, spec.axe)?` in the form build (~bundle.rs:3949); (2) a `MANIAXE_AXE_FRAMES: [PlayerFrameDescriptor; 4]` const; (3) `ActiveProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe` (types.rs) + the trace.rs arm; (4) a scene.rs `ManiaxeAxe` draw arm reading the Maniaxe form's `axe` frames via `select_player_form_visuals`/`forms.get`, falling back to the green rect. Verify with a deterministic scene test (ManiaxeAxe projectile → asserts a `Sprite` command, not the green `Rect`) + a Maniaxe-throw capture-frames. **Blocker for a verified landing this session:** the four `pfd(origin_x, origin_y, width_px, height_px)` values must be decoded from the 0x0A589E mappings (the existing Maniaxe pfd constants were hand-derived from ROM mappings, not the manifest) — shipping guessed offsets would be a fidelity guess, so deferred rather than committed blind.

### #324

**REGRESSION — hit/shaking blocks suppress the foreground terrain (a tree) underneath, showing blank background.** Suspect commits `796ae7503` "Hide terrain under active prize block wobble" (2026-06-15) + `50ad4a6ee` "Hide terrain under live block cells" (2026-06-17).

- Kid Chameleon stores **foreground tile layout** and **block layout** as two separate planes (`.cache/upstream/kid-chameleon-disasm/doc/formats.txt:73-74`); a block can overlay a decorated foreground cell (tree). The renderer historically drew extracted foreground terrain then composited block art over it, so foreground showed behind/around blocks.
- `796ae7503` added `if active_block_bounce { continue; }` in `push_level_layout_terrain` (scene.rs ~3668) — the SHAKE path: during the prize wobble the sprite is offset by `y_offset` (scene.rs:3809,3859), so as it shakes the now-suppressed foreground leaves the cell showing sky/background instead of the tree. `50ad4a6ee` widened it to `|| live_cell.is_some_and(|cell| cell.has_block)` (scene.rs:3674), removing the underlay under static blocks too.
- Both commits were tuned to kill a hell-theme level-06 right-edge residual for #289, not validated on forest blocks over tree art. **Their cited ASM labels (`sub_302F6`/`sub_3034A` in 50ad4a6ee, `sub_1007A` foreground-update-queue claim in 796ae7503) do NOT exist in the cached disasm** (kid.asm has no 30xxx labels and no sub_1007A), so the suppression's fidelity is unproven.
- **Fix:** reproduce on a forest level (capture-frames during a block shake over tree foreground); re-derive whether the ROM block fully overwrites the Scroll-A cell or whether foreground decoration is a distinct visible plane (formats.txt's two-plane split argues the latter); likely narrow/revert both `continue` guards and re-evaluate the #289 hell residual with a level-06-specific repro. Not a #149 wobble-sprite regression — the wobble sprite is still drawn (scene.rs:3854); the missing element is the foreground terrain UNDER it.
- **Investigation 2026-06-18 (latest+19, stays `[ ]` — no code, deliberately NOT blind-fixed).** Confirmed the **data** model: the map header carries SEPARATE 32-bit pointers for "foreground tile layout" and "block layout" (formats.txt:73-74), so a block and a decorated foreground cell are distinct source data. But the **render** question — at a cell holding both, does the ROM's Scroll-A nametable show the block (foreground overwritten at load) or composite the block sprite over a still-visible foreground tile? — is empirical and CANNOT be answered from the cached disasm (the suspect commits' `sub_302F6`/`sub_3034A`/`sub_1007A` labels are absent). The current guards (revert candidates) and #289's hell-theme residual pull in OPPOSITE directions, so a blind revert risks re-opening the closed #289. This is a "compare oracle frames, do not guess" case: it needs jgenesis frames of a forest level with a block over tree decoration during a hit/wobble, diffed against native, BEFORE touching the two `continue` guards. Deferred to a session that can drive that oracle repro; recorded here so the next session does not blind-revert from the two-plane argument alone.
- **Fixed candidate 2026-06-18 (latest+21, `[ ]`→`[?]`).** Corrected the stale investigation premise: the cited labels **are present** in the cached disasm (`sub_1007A`, `sub_302F6`, `sub_3034A`). ASM `sub_1007A` rewrites the live `Level_Layout` cell to `$6Fxx` while drawing copied block art as an object; `sub_302F6`/`sub_3034A` consume the live Scroll-A cell words. The native renderer also has the extracted foreground tile-layout plane listed separately from the block layout in `formats.txt`, and level 0 provides a concrete overlap: Blue Lake Woods 1 prize block `(57,1)` has foreground skin `$1B` underneath live `$E102`. Narrowed the fix by removing the terrain-pass suppression for active/live block cells, while special-casing active prize-bounce `$6Fxx` cells so terrain uses the immutable foreground skin instead of the temporary `$6F` live-cell skin. The copied prize-block wobble object still draws on top from the live block path. Regression coverage: `build_scene_draws_prize_block_wobble_sprite_even_after_deleted_cell_write`, `build_scene_draws_live_prize_block_wobble_from_block_skin_not_terrain`, `foreground_layout_terrain_keeps_separate_foreground_under_live_block_cells_loc_302f6`, and the `foreground_layout_terrain` group. Re-ran the #289 level-06 recording that motivated `50ad4a6ee`: the command still exits non-zero because the stored native trace is stale at frame 0, but oracle state matched and the frame residual improved to 30 pixels / MAE 0.020898437 at both sampled frames 60 and 179 (bounds x=275..279,y=151..161). Keep `[?]` until a human hits a forest block over tree art in play-native and confirms no blank background during wobble.

### #325

**REGRESSION — Highwater waterfall (level 02/03) turned light-blue and stopped animating; water "looks bad" on a later level.** Suspect commit `9757cf94b` "Seed live level palette buffer" (2026-06-16).

- Two-stage water palette cycle: (1) seed Palette_Buffer from the foreground theme palette (ASM Load_InGame `loc_11DB0`); (2) `RotatePalette_Lava_Water loc_1223C` rotates words $E/$10/$12/$14 each cycle. Stage (1) is dead on real assets.
- `load_level_theme_palettes_loc_11db0_11e16` (crates/kid-core/src/level.rs:17979-17996) builds the path as `format!("palette_fg/{foreground_theme}.bin")` with `foreground_theme = header.level_theme` (a `u8`, trace.rs:678) → requests `palette_fg/7.bin` (Mountain) or `palette_fg/8.bin` (Cave). But the extraction manifest names palette assets by THEME NAME: `palette_fg/mountain.bin`, `palette_fg/cave.bin`, `palette_fg/island.bin` (verified in `.cache/generated/<sha>/asset-manifest.json` + on disk; no numeric `7.bin`/`8.bin`). `theme_palette_words` (level.rs:17937) does an exact `relative_path` match → `None` → `copy_foreground_palette_loc_11DB0` (level.rs:8619) never runs → Palette_Buffer words 7..10 never get real water colours.
- Downstream: the rotator (`rotate_palette_lava_water_loc_1223C` level.rs:9295, ticked lib.rs:4620 — both faithful to ASM kid.asm:24373-24384) rotates zero/junk; trace shows `lava_water_palette_words_loc_1223c=[0,0,0,0]` (already observed live in a #289 archive note). Renderer `foreground_palette_for_scene` (scene.rs:2282-2311) guards path-1 on `words.any(!=0)`, fails, and takes the legacy fallback (scene.rs:2303) that rotates the extracted asset palette with a hardcoded `+2` pre-advance tuned only for Highwater's direct level-skip lineage and steps every 5/8 frames → wrong base colour (light blue) + near-static.
- **Fix:** map theme id → name when building the palette path (also affects the bg path), OR emit numeric aliases at extraction; replace the masking synthetic `palette_fg/7.bin` fixture (`begin_level_entry_seeds_theme_palette_buffer_loc_11db0_11e16`, level_tests.rs:3243-3250) with the real name-based path; add a regression asserting `lava_water_palette_words_loc_1223c` is non-zero + rotating on Highwater. Dead ends: core rotation maths / Island band cycle (loc_12098/12110/12188) are faithful and untouched; the #308/#309 recent window did not touch palette code. Fixing this unblocks the live loc_1223C path that #289/#215/#280 depend on.
- **RESOLVED 2026-06-18 (latest+19, `[ ]`→`[?]`, commit 302d51b51).** Added `theme_palette_basename(theme)` (level.rs) reusing the ROM-ordered `THEME_COLLISION_FILES_LOC_11C30` name table (mountain.bin/cave.bin/island.bin… — identical basenames to the palette assets, same order as kid-render `THEME_NAMES`). `load_level_theme_palettes_loc_11db0_11e16` now resolves BOTH fg (`palette_fg/{name}`) and bg (`palette_bg/{name}`) paths through it; the cave/city override arms are unchanged. Replaced the masking numeric `palette_fg/7.bin`/`palette_bg/4.bin` fixtures in the two `begin_level_entry…` palette tests with `palette_fg/mountain.bin`/`palette_bg/island.bin` (theme 7=mountain, 4=island). New `theme_palette_basename_maps_theme_id_to_name_not_number` pins the mapping; new real-asset `highwater_entry_seeds_nonzero_lava_water_words_loc_11db0_1223c` (`cached_generated_runtime`, level 0x02 = theme 0x07 mountain) asserts the loc_1223C band is non-zero — green on real assets, so loc_11DB0 now seeds real water colours. `verify-slice-fast` green (6135+9). ### #326

**Title cards for levels ≥ hex 0x10 draw the wrong name** (the Cyclone/demo level Skydragon Castle 1 / logical 0x1B shows "Caves of Ice").

- `AddrTbl_LevelNames` index comments in `level/levelnames.asm` are HEX (`; 1B`, `; 27` — same convention as `maporder.asm` / `doc/level_list.txt` logical-id column). `parse_level_name_comment_id` (crates/kid-data/src/lib.rs:5221) calls `parse_asm_integer` first, which for an unprefixed token does `str::parse` = decimal (lib.rs:1490), and only falls back to base-16 when decimal parse *fails*. A bare `27` is valid decimal, so it never reaches the hex fallback → keys to decimal 27 = 0x1B. Result: TitleText_27 ("caves of ice") stored under title_card[0x1B]; TitleText_39 ("forbidden tombs") under 0x27; etc. The whole table from hex 0x10 up is skewed.
- Surfaces via demo 2 = Skydragon Castle 1 (demo.rs:90 `DEMO_2_LEVEL=0x1B`, the Cyclone-helmet level); `rebuild_starting_level_title_workers` (movement.rs:2064) reads title_card[0x1B] = the mis-keyed "caves of ice" glyphs. Manifest decode confirms title_card[0x1B] → "caves|of|ice", title_card[0x27] → "forbidden tombs", while the ROM has TitleText_1B "skydragon castle" / TitleText_27 "caves of ice".

### #327

**Teleporter wrongly shows the level-load title-card / loader screen before warping.** ASM-traced, actionable; splits the loader sub-symptom out of #298/#300. (Reproduces since #300 wired the live teleport transition; flagged in the 2026-06-14 NOW block.)

- ROM trace: `loc_BCF6` (kid.asm:15275-15280) sets `$FFFFFC29` then `bra.w Teleport`. `Teleport` (kid.asm:14787-14789): `tst.b FC29; bne +; move.w #8,(Game_Mode)` — FC29 is set, so Game_Mode is NOT changed; it stays $000C (in-gameplay value from loc_1AE2E, kid.asm:29062). `loc_6E2` → `LoadGameModeData` indexes `GameLoadArray` by Game_Mode: $8 = Load_TitleCard, $C = Load_InGame (kid.asm:23570-23573). So teleporters reload via **Load_InGame, no title card** — only Pal_FadeOut + `#$EE` warp colour (FBCC) + sfx_Teleport.
- The same/cross distinction is `$FFFFFC36` (set only on the cross-level `loc_BCEA` branch, kid.asm:15273); FC36 just resets the timer/bonus flags (Init_Timer_and_Bonus_Flags, kid.asm:6551-6557) — it does NOT gate the loader. **So neither same- nor cross-level teleporters should show the title card** — the human's belief that cross-level "should show the loader" does not match the ROM.
- Native bug: `combat.rs:12847-12848` routes same-level teleports to `begin_level_entry` → `BootState::StartingLevel` (level.rs:18556) + `rebuild_starting_level_title_workers` (level.rs:18654); StartingLevel renders the title-card VDP (lib.rs:2290-2295). Native applied the DEATH/respawn rationale (lose_life → Game_Mode=$8 → Load_TitleCard) to teleporters, but `lose_life` (kid.asm:14763-14770) never sets FC29 whereas teleporters always do — opposite Game_Mode outcome.
- **Fix:** introduce a Load_InGame-style teleport re-entry (Game_Mode $C semantics) that bypasses the title-card shell, keeping the loc_11BD2 PlayerStart override, FBCC=$EE fade, sfx_Teleport; the cross-level case adds only the FC36 timer/bonus reset. Then flip `live_same_level_teleporter_reloads_level_entry_loc_bcf6` (combat_tests.rs:2386) — its `BootState::StartingLevel` assertion + comment encode the ASM misread. Confirm death/respawn still shows the card. Not a regression (no recent commit touched it); #298 block-list/countdown plumbing and #300 MapOrder destination are correct — this is purely the post-warp Game_Mode/boot-state dispatch.
- **RESOLVED 2026-06-18 (latest+19, `[ ]`→`[?]`, commit dcccc2115).** Refactored `begin_level_entry` (level.rs) to compute the title-card boot-state up front, then delegate the level-load body to a new shared `load_level_entry_common(level_id, entered_from_live_gameplay)` (block grid, theme palettes, entry fade, opening slice, rosters, murder wall, weather, post-load objects, start BGM, per-level counters). Added `begin_teleport_level_entry_load_ingame_loc_bcf6` that sets `BootState::InGame`, calls the shared loader, clears the title-worker shell, and clears the loc_11BD2 override. `check_teleporter_contact`'s same-level branch (combat.rs:12847) now calls it instead of `begin_level_entry`. Because the InGame entry fade (`step_allow_pausing_fade_sub_73d0`, lib.rs) already runs under `BootState::InGame` while `!allow_pausing`, the teleport fade animates correctly there; the trace's `teleport_warp_colour` gate (trace.rs) gained `InGame && !allow_pausing` so FBCC=$00EE stays visible during the fade, and the fade-complete arm now clears `teleport_warp_colour_fbcc` (the old StartingLevel→InGame hand-off cleared it at boot.rs:7449, which the no-card path skips — without this a later death respawn would re-tint its black fade yellow). **Cross-level confirmed already correct:** `pending_level_skip` → `enter_level_skip_hold` sets `BootState::LevelSkipHold` (the level-skip wipe), never the title card, so the FC36 cross-level branch needed no change. Flipped 3 tests encoding the StartingLevel misread: `live_same_level_teleporter_reloads_level_entry_loc_bcf6` (combat_tests), `live_telepad_warps_only_after_90_grounded_frames_loc_b522` + `blue_lake_woods_2_teleporter_uses_generated_block_list_loc_b522_loc_bc80` (runtime_tests) — all now assert `BootState::InGame` + empty title workers. The hundred-K-trip end-credits teleport (loc_DA4A) still uses `begin_level_entry` (out of scope, separate transition). `verify-slice-fast` green (6134); `verify-tas-full` running. Human to confirm the BLW2 telepad shows no card and death/respawn still does, hence `[?]`.

### #328

**NOT A BUG / ORIGINAL_QUIRK — Cyclone flight "straight up / no tornado spin / too powerful".** Player expectation diverges from the original design on both points.

- **No lateral/tornado motion in the ROM.** `sub_B168`/`loc_B214` (kid.asm:14091-14126) mutates only `y_vel(a3)` (Cyclone_YAcceleration +$400 gravity, −$3000 C-thrust on the `bclr` rising edge, clamp). The visible "tornado spin" is a 3-frame sprite animation in `sub_B270`/`loc_B2A0` (kid.asm:14154-14174, indexes LnkTo_unk_BA55A) — no x_vel term. Horizontal movement is normal air x-control. Native reproduces the spin (helmets.rs:701-728) and leaves x-control to normal physics (lib.rs:3753-3756, cyclone_flying gates only gravity).
- **No altitude/fuel/duration cap.** Activation (`loc_ACB0` kid.asm:13511, `loc_A830` kid.asm:13137) sets `Cyclone_flying` on a C rising edge with zero cost; flight gives a fresh −$3000 per rising edge capped at −$30000 (3px/frame, `loc_B25E` kid.asm:14119). The flag clears only on landing/floor-loss (`sf (Cyclone_flying)`). Spamming C rises without limit in the genuine ROM. Native matches: constants.rs:774-786 equal the ROM literals; step_cyclone_flight (helmets.rs:5354-5432) + step_cyclone_activation (helmets.rs:5445-5459) implement rising-edge thrust (#084), wrapping arithmetic (#085), after-physics activation, and the clamp.
- **One cheap human check (needs_human_repro):** if a live build lets Kid keep rising on a single *held* C (no re-tap), that WOULD diverge from the ROM rising-edge model → reopen. The code reads rising-edge correct (`input.c && !previous_input.c`). Not a regression (#076/#084/#085 archived [x], constants unchanged since the types.rs/constants.rs extraction refactor). Mark native with `// ORIGINAL_QUIRK`.

### #329

**Leftover/aliased warp targets skip with a foreground-parse error.** `play-native`'s debug warp printed `skipping debug warp target …: failed to parse … foreground layout: foreground layout length 7838 does not match expected 6720 (80x84 cells)` for logical `0x47` ("The Crypt (leftover)") and `0x38`.

- Root cause: `load_level_visuals` (`crates/kid-render/src/bundle.rs`) resolved the foreground **bytes** and **geometry** from different levels. Geometry came from `visual_theme_header` (the mapped *resource* header, ASM `loc_11A50`); bytes came from `load_level_asset_bundle` which is `resource.foreground.or(logical.foreground)`. For `0x47`→resource `0x42` ("Alien Twilight", no foreground), bytes fell back to logical `0x47` (`7838` B) but dims came from resource `0x42` (`4×6 = 6720`). `7838 ≠ 6720` and not a coherent multiple of the resource width → `ForegroundLayout::parse` bailed → warp skipped.
- The block-grid/collision path already commits to resource geometry and truncates: `decode_level_layout` (`crates/kid-core/src/level.rs`) computes `expected_cells` from the resource header, reads the logical level's decoded terrain, and keeps the first `expected_cells` bytes when `terrain_bytes.len() >= expected_cells`. Affected levels have `height_flag_bits = 0` (`blank_top_rows = 0`), so the render's expected size equals the collision grid's `expected_cells`.
- **Fix (`[ ]`→`[?]`):** keep resource geometry (NOT logical — that would make the render disagree with the already-correct collision grid and is less faithful to `loc_11A50`), but detect the borrowed-logical case (resource has no foreground of its own) and truncate the foreground bytes to `width_screens*20 * height_screens*14` before parsing, mirroring `decode_level_layout`. Gated to the borrowed case only, so non-aliased levels keep the parser's exact/±5-tolerance/height-inference behaviour. Single function changed; no parser or terrain-decoder edits.
- Regression: `load_level_visuals_truncates_borrowed_logical_foreground_to_resource_grid_loc_11a50` (kid-render) builds an aliased level whose resource has no foreground and a smaller header; asserts load succeeds, geometry equals the resource grid, and parsed cells equal the first `expected` bytes of the borrowed logical foreground. The two existing aliased tests stay green (their resource alias IS in `decoded_levels` / has its own foreground → no truncation).
- Smoke (real generated manifest): `0x47`/`0x38` now LOAD (were SKIP); `0x41` still skips (`no foreground layout data` — genuinely has no foreground); `0x39` loads via the pre-dumped `level-layout` fixture in this cache. **Mode B remains open (separate item):** when the `level-layout` fixture is absent, `0x39/0x32/0x2D/0x2B/0x29` reach `decode_level_layout`'s strict `>= expected_cells` and fail because the resource foreground is ~2 bytes short of its own header (the render path uses ±5 tolerance) — a separate asymmetry, untouched here.
- Verified: `cargo test -p kid-render load_level_visuals` (5 pass) + `parse_foreground` (4 pass); `mise run verify-slice-fast` green (6145 pass). Human validation: warp to `0x47`/`0x38` and confirm the foreground renders coherently aligned with collision.
- **2026-06-18 follow-up — Mode B1 fixed (collision side):** human warp-through (Mac, no `level-layout` fixtures) confirmed `0x47`/`0x38` stopped skipping but surfaced the remaining block-grid skips for `0x29/0x2B/0x2D/0x32/0x39` (`missing generated level layout … and native terrain decode failed`). These hit `decode_level_layout` (no fixture). Mirror of #329's render fix, now on the collision side: `decode_level_layout` (`crates/kid-core/src/level.rs`) gained `resolve_terrain_to_expected_cells_loc_11C34`, which zero-pads a terrain buffer short by ≤5 bytes to `expected_cells` (the same ±5 tolerance `ForegroundLayout::parse` already applies and zero-pads), instead of the strict `< expected_cells` reject. Resolves **Mode B1**: `0x2B`(res `0x3B`, −5), `0x2D`(res `0x33`, −2), `0x32`(res `0x38`, −2), `0x39`(res `0x47`, −2) — all foreground a few trailing bytes short of the resource header's cell count. Larger shortfalls still return None. Tests: pure `terrain_length_tolerance` unit group (exact/longer/short-≤5-pads/7838-of-7840/short->5-rejects) + cache-gated `decode_level_layout_tolerates_short_leftover_foreground_loc_11c34` (asserts `0x2B/0x2D/0x32/0x39` decode to a grid matching the resource header geometry with a solid floor). End-to-end smoke: `0x32` (no fixture locally) now LOADS via decode. `verify-slice-fast` green (6151). `// UNVERIFIED`: the genuine ROM tail for these unreachable levels reads adjacent RAM, not 0 — there is no oracle for levels normal play never loads, so this matches the render's zero-pad.
- **Mode B2 still OPEN (separate item):** `0x29` (res `0x31`, `height_flag_bits=1` → `blank_top_rows=2`) skips on the no-fixture path for a *different* reason — its foreground is exactly 6720 but `decode_level_layout` inflates `expected_cells` by `blank_top_rows*width` (240), so the shortfall (240 ≫ 5) is not the tolerance case. The decode path bakes `blank_top_rows` into the read height passed to `level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` rather than building populated rows then shifting via `insert_blank_top_rows_sub_140F6`; fixing that faithfully is a larger geometry change (risks the byte-exact fidelity test) — deferred. `0x41` also still skips (genuinely has no foreground at all).

- **#337 (player/forms, `[ ]`→`[?]`)** — FIXED candidate 2026-06-19 (implementation session). Root cause confirmed: in the ROM `Maniaxe_throwing_axe` is SET at throw (loc_76E4) and NEVER cleared by the axe object's lifecycle (ManiaxeAxe_Init/loc_8A52/loc_8ABC/loc_8ACC/loc_8AF2 only Delete_CurrentObject); it is cleared ONLY by the Kid's per-frame state dispatch — `sub_78E8 loc_794C` (grounded/standing) AND `sub_942A loc_9454` (airborne/walking), both gated on the throw-anim-done flag `$18(a3)`. Native modelled only the grounded clear (`refresh_grounded_helmet_state_sub_78E8`, run from lib.rs ONLY while `on_ground`) plus the absent-projectile clear (helmets.rs:6630). So an airborne Kid whose boomerang axe (loc_8A74 reverses every 12 frames) oscillates inside the camera-padded out-of-bounds box (loc_8B32) never culls, the absent-projectile clear never fires, and the grounded latch never ticks → the gate stays latched and every further throw is blocked. **Fix (single-dispatch, avoids the spec's hazard):** the original prepare-the-fix proposal added the airborne tick INSIDE `step_maniaxe_axe` (pre-physics) gated on `!on_ground`; the adversarial verify flagged that this double-decrements on a landing frame (airborne pre-physics + grounded post-physics both tick → 1-frame-early release). Verified the hazard is real — `step_maniaxe_axe` runs pre-physics (lib.rs:3773), `refresh_grounded_helmet_state_sub_78E8` runs post-physics gated on `on_ground` (lib.rs:4652). So instead the airborne tick is added as a NEW method `tick_maniaxe_airborne_throw_latch_loc_9454` (helmets.rs) wired as the `else` of the post-physics `if on_ground` dispatch (lib.rs:4654) — exactly ONE of grounded/airborne runs per frame (post-physics on_ground), matching the ROM's single mutually-exclusive branch per frame, so the latch decrements exactly once per frame with no double-tick. The method is Maniaxe-only and only touches the latch/gate. Regression `airborne_helmet_state_sub_942a_releases_maniaxe_gate_loc_9454` (projectile_tests.rs): throw grounded, go airborne with the axe still live, tick the airborne method 17× → gate clears, axe stays flying, a 2nd throw succeeds; verified RED with the method no-op'd. The 17-frame latch is the same `MANIAXE_THROW_LATCH_FRAMES_LOC_794C` (stru_8B4E grounded 3+2+2+$A=17 and stru_8B60 airborne 5+$C=17 are both 17). Grounded path unchanged: 49 maniaxe + 22 sub_78e8 tests still green. NUANCE: the ROM's true dispatch discriminator is standing (x_vel==0) vs moving (x_vel!=0), spanning both grounded and airborne — native approximates with on_ground; the latch result is identical because every branch does the same decrement, so the on_ground-based split is functionally correct for the gate. Gameplay-affecting; `verify-slice-fast` + `verify-tas-full` run before commit. No Maniaxe oracle scenario exists (#337 caveat), so human playtest validation (throw-jump rapidly, confirm firing never locks out) is the remaining gate → `[?]`.

The native START already POOLS both variants into one recomputed refcount (a deliberate simplification of the ROM's two-slot/one-sfx scheme), so the symmetric STOP is **edge detection on that pooled count**, not the per-object helper: `refresh_active_roster` snapshots `driving_rock_tank_count()` before the frame's activations/death-removals and calls `stop_rock_tank_drive_sound_on_last_exit_loc_3c46e(before)` → `queue_play_sound2(TankDriving)` on the `>0 → 0` edge. `remove_dead_enemy` already drops a corpse only once its death animation finishes, matching the ROM's post-hibernate decrement timing; the pre-existing pure helper `deactivation_drive_sound_cleanup_loc_3C494` (test-only) stays as the per-object ASM spec — its single `wrapping_sub(1)` can't express native's batch removal, so it's documentation not the wiring. Removed the now-live `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `queue_play_sound2` (lib.rs) and `QueuedSoundCommand::PlaySound2` (combat.rs). **Tests** (runtime_tests.rs): `loc_3c46e_last_rock_tank_exit_emits_playsound2_tank_driving_stop` (1→0 emits `PlaySound2(TankDriving)`, NOT PlaySound), `loc_3c4a8_drive_stop_holds_while_another_rock_tank_remains` (2→1 silent; proves pooling Tank+TankShooting), `loc_3c46e_drive_stop_silent_when_no_rock_tank_was_driving` (0 before → silent), `driving_rock_tank_count_excludes_unlatched_tanks_and_other_families`. **Gates:** `verify-slice-fast` 6183+9 green; full sweep 0-104 tier state + `verify-tas-full` green (sound is advisory/CRC-neutral). Discovery via a 4-agent Explore workflow (start-wiring / despawn-plumbing / asm-stop-semantics / sound-api+tests). **UNVERIFIED (#264 caveat):** whether `PlaySound2($1F)` audibly *halts* vs *restarts* the GEMS loop can't be confirmed headless — human to validate the drone stops when the last RockTank scrolls off/dies. `[?]` pending that audio check.
- **#339 (audio, `[ ]`)** — REFINED 2026-06-19 (implementation session): the START is wired (loc_3B40A/loc_3B690, enemies.rs:10188-10243). The STOP belongs at the DESPAWN path: ASM `loc_3C46E`→`loc_3C4A8` (kid.asm:43991) does `subi.b #1,(a4,d7.w)` on the shared `$FFFFFA34+object_meta` refcount and, on zero, `jsr j_PlaySound2` with `byte_3C46C[d6]` (=`sfx_Tank_driving` for Tank). Native despawn is `active.retain(...)` in `activate_enemies_with_rng_inner` (enemies.rs:9903), whose own comment (9899-9901) admits "sound cleanup is managed separately" — but it is NOT. The fix needs real plumbing: thread the sound queue (+ a persistent drive-active flag / per-type refcount) into the despawn path and emit the stop when the last driving Tank is removed. It is the **PlaySound2** (bank-2) path, distinct from the PlaySound START; `played_sound_effects: Vec<QueuedSoundEffect>` models only PlaySound, so the stop must use `queue_play_sound2`/`QueuedSoundCommand::PlaySound2`, and whether PlaySound2(TankDriving) halts vs restarts the GEMS loop needs a real audio device to confirm (#264 caveat).
