## 2026-06-20 #083 floor-landing sub-pixel hypothesis (migrated schema example)

- Migrated from the now-removed `hypotheses/floor_landing_subpixel.toml`. This was
  the only worked example of the `test-hypothesis` TOML schema; preserved here so
  the schema and the original framing survive folder deletion.
- Finding (as framed before #083 was resolved): when Kid lands on floor with
  `y_vel >= 0` (falling), the sub-pixel low word might be preserved by ASM
  `loc_AAF8` (`move.w d7,y_pos` preserves the low word), but `sub_902A` also zeroes
  the sub-pixel (`clr.w $20`) when floor-snapping. The hypothesis was: which path
  does the oracle take at frame 955 of `kc_any_percent_2024`? #083 later resolved
  this: `sub_902A` (kid.asm:10462) always does `clr.w $20(a3)` on new floor
  landings (airborne -> grounded), zeroing the sub-pixel; the low word is only
  preserved when already grounded (sub_902A exits early via loc_913A when
  `y_vel=0`).
- Consumer: `test-hypothesis <path>` consumes this TOML format via an explicit
  path argument (it is NOT auto-discovered from any folder). The full original
  file is reproduced below as the canonical schema example.

```toml
[hypothesis]
name = "floor_landing_preserves_subpixel_when_falling"
description = """
When kid lands on floor with y_vel >= 0 (falling), sub-pixel should be
preserved in ASM (loc_AAF8: move.w d7,y_pos preserves low word).
However sub_902A also zeroes sub-pixel (clr.w $20) when floor-snapping.
Need to determine which path the oracle takes at frame 955."""
scenario = "kc_any_percent_2024"
frame_range = [954, 956]

[oracle]
watches = ["0xFF24FE:u32", "0xFF2502:i32", "0xFF2500:u16"]
# 0xFF24FE = kid_y_pos (full 32-bit), 0xFF2502 = kid_y_vel, 0xFF2500 = kid_y_pos sub-pixel word

[assertions]
# Oracle y_pos at frame 955 should have non-zero sub-pixel
oracle_955_subpixel = "0xFF2500_u16[955] != 0"

[comparison]
native_field = "kid_y_pos"
oracle_address = "0xFF24FE"
frame = 955
```

## 2026-06-20 playtest triage

Source: a single ~28-symptom human playthrough ("latest pushed changes"), cross-referenced against the backlog table + `backlog-archive.md` + the 68k disassembly by a 29-agent workflow (one investigator per symptom + a synthesis pass). Docs-only. The human's "issues keep getting missed or denied" complaint is accurate; it decomposes into four anti-patterns: (A) **denied-by-parking** — `[?]` treated as done across many playtests; (B) **missed start-without-stop wiring** — stop helpers ported as `#[cfg(not(test))]` dead code; (C) **parked-with-gate-unmet** — a `[?]` fix's own "human retest" gate treated as satisfied; (D) **missed-by-keyword-deflection** — triagers land on closed projectile/probe rows. A cross-cutting cause: several "green" tests assert MODEL state or use a native-as-oracle audit, so they pass while the human-visible RENDER/PITCH defect goes undetected.

### Reopens (fresh human repro = the validation the `[?]`/`[b]` awaited, and it failed)

- **#264 (audio/perf, `[?]`→`[ ]`)** — REOPEN 2026-06-20. BGM stutter / "every other sound slows", most reliably as Iron Knight jumping on a metal block. Triggers are ASM-correct and wired (metal-block $12 `loc_110D0` kid.asm:23021 → blocks.rs:3592; diamond $2D `loc_2510C` kid.asm:21101 → combat.rs:9635) — NOT a trigger gap. Root cause is static: audio is generated synchronously inside the video loop (native_player/mod.rs:801, `gems.generate_samples(735)`) and pushed to an SDL queue capped at `AUDIO_QUEUE_TARGET_FRAMES=2` (mod.rs:39); a long/SFX-burst frame drops the generated frame (`record_skipped_full_frame`, mod.rs:844) or starves SDL → BGM samples drop. Parked across ≥5 playtests (06-08/-11/-13/-16/-19), each pass tweaking the 2-vs-3 cap and re-blocking on "needs a real audio device". STOP tweaking the cap; the durable fix is to decouple audio generation from the video frame loop (audio thread / SDL callback pulling a ring buffer, or generate-ahead with an underrun guard). Pair with #341 oracle injection so retests are measurable. Owner of the audio-slowdown family (#216/#272/#003 cross-link).
- **#272 (audio, `[?]`→`[ ]`)** — REOPEN 2026-06-20. DAC voices low/deep: death ($60 — sounds like a groan not "die"), Samurai attack ($13 "hoi"), somersault/jump-on-enemy ($4C), helmet-pickup/transform ($2E). - [Verify] 2026-06-20 fixed candidate: real jgenesis event-window reports confirmed the systematic native pitch error, then verified the fix. Root cause was standalone GEMS timing, not sound triggers or host resampling: the Z80 driver used YM2612 timer/status reads to pace DACME, but native advanced that shadow by Z80 cycles and kept hidden init-frame event timestamps while the mixer timeline started at sample zero. Fix: advance the standalone GEMS YM2612 shadow at the YM input clock (`YM2612_INPUT_CLOCK_HZ / Z80_CLOCK_HZ`) with a fractional accumulator, and reset the hidden init audio-event epoch after the `$0B` pointer-init frames before visible playback starts. Verification artefacts: `verify-native-audio-output-file --scenario .cache/recordings/issue272-red-stealth-air-attack-direct-current/scenario.json` writes `.cache/oracle-runs/issue272-red-stealth-air-attack-direct-native-audio/audio-event-oracle-windows.json`, where `$13` reports 641 Hz native vs 638 Hz jgenesis. `verify-native-audio-output-file --scenario .cache/recordings/issue272-level01-redstealth-r0-25-b24-64/scenario.json` writes `.cache/oracle-runs/idle_level_01-native-audio/audio-event-oracle-windows.json`, covering `$60`, `$13`, `$46`, and `$66` in the same pitch range as jgenesis after the fix. Focused regressions: `standalone_gems_converts_z80_cycles_to_ym2612_input_clocks`, `gems_engine_init_resets_hidden_boot_audio_event_epoch`, and `audio_event_oracle_window_reports_compare_matching_frame_windows`. Fixed candidate 2026-06-29: the 2026-06-26 post-death/card report sharpened the remaining #339 leak to same-frame native playback ordering, not a missing Tank deactivation edge. ASM `Load_InGame loc_23629` calls `j_StopMusic` before `loc_11FD2/loc_12004` queues level BGM, so any stale Tank SFX delta that native condenses into that same cold `InGame` trace frame is pre-reset state. Native already emitted `StopMusicThenStart(bgm)` for cold level cues, but `native_bgm_command_suppresses_same_frame_sfx` only suppressed same-frame SFX on `LevelTransition`; `StartSequence($1F)` / `StartSequence($3C)` could therefore replay after the reset in `play-native`/recorded audio events. Fix: pass the active cue into the suppression predicate and suppress same-frame SFX for `StopMusicThenStart` only when `active_before=None` and the trace is `InGame`/`DemoPlay`, preserving ordinary active-cue level replacements such as options-to-gameplay block SFX. ### #25

Retired 2026-06-21 (GitHub issue #25, "frame-951 RUSTFLAGS-sensitive divergence / latent UB"): NOT REPRODUCIBLE on `main` (9b284ceb3). The `.mise.toml` caveats claimed that building TAS replay with `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings` produced a binary diverging at any-percent-published frame 951 (`kid_y_vel +0x4001` vs `+0x4000` during wall-cling right), suspected latent UB or a hidden cfg. Phase-0 reproduction: clean A/B build into the same `./target` — plain `cargo build --release -p wildside-cli` vs `RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo build --release`. The strict build genuinely recompiled (3m20s vs a 0.13s no-op, so the fingerprint differed and `-D warnings` was applied) yet produced a **byte-identical** binary (both SHA1 `6fa0d85e3ecee5bde48da85312bcc51c2848e3d8`). Replaying the strict binary over frames 0..1000 at `checkpoint_interval=1` (covers 951): CRC matches all 1000 frames; `divergence_summary` authoritative/accumulation/rng all 0; no `first_crc_mismatch`; at frame 951 native `kid_y_vel == oracle == -132640` (the clean `+0x4000` increment from frame 950's `-149024`). Conclusion: the original observation was a **stale/mixed incremental-build-cache heisenbug**, not a codegen-sensitive bug. `-D warnings` is a lint level and does not change codegen when compilation succeeds.

Dead ends (do NOT re-attempt): (1) the issue's lead probe `overflow-checks=true` — the velocity pipeline is uniformly `saturating_add`/`clamp`/`.min`/`.max` (physics.rs:584,788-799), no signed-overflow path, and a clean i32 overflow wraps by a power of two, not the observed +1 LSB; (2) Miri/ASAN at the FFI boundary — all 11 `unsafe` blocks are YM2612 audio FFI in `ymfm-sys`, `wildside-core` has zero `unsafe`/`MaybeUninit`/floats, and audio output cannot feed Kid's y-velocity in a deterministic engine; (3) "hidden cfg" — no `cfg!(debug_assertions)`/`cfg!(test)`/`option_env!` gameplay branch exists for RUSTFLAGS to toggle. Note: the `+0x4001`/`frame 951` figures are real (verbatim in `.mise.toml`, not fabricated — an early grep missed them by searching only `docs/`+`crates/`).

Outcome: the three stale `.mise.toml` caveats (verify-tas-frontier, view-tas, verify-tas-full) rewritten to the verified finding — no-strict-rust is kept because clippy is the warning authority (#24 step 1) and setting RUSTFLAGS would fork a redundant release cache, not for determinism. This unblocks #24 step 4 (TAS-profile unification). Reproduction artefacts under `.cache/frame951/` (untracked).

## 2026-06-25 playtest triage

Source: human voice playtest, build = last pushed commit `253e98961` (origin/main, "wire Driller
collision dispatch (#32)", 2026-06-25), which **contains all the 2026-06-23 fixed candidates**. 17 distinct observations parsed and
cross-referenced against the lanes + ASM + code by a fan-out research pass. Build identity is the
key fact: because the candidates were in the build, the ones still broken **failed validation**.

### Build-confirmed fixed-candidate FAILURES (reopened `[?]`→`[ ]` into the open queue)

- **#210 / #254 (intro skip).** Skipping the intro still shows black/garbled graphics instead of
  the title / Red-Stealth pose. The 2026-06-23 candidates (`5fc130013` carry VDP across skips,
  `a9620dc14`/`77929c6b4`/`4624f6434` direct-title workers) FAILED. Known anti-pattern risk
  recorded earlier: the fix tends to latch onto specific probe-frame constants
  (`INTRO_SEQUENCE_6_FAST_RESTORE_CARRY_LAST_READY_FRAME=2510`, tests pinned to Start at
  2400/2450/2500), so a live Start at an unprobed frame still garbles. Next step is engine-level:

  kid.asm:31119 jumps straight to `$2C`/`loc_6E2`/`Load_TitleScreen`), no frame constants. Do NOT
  retune CRAM/d2 for the title fade (rejected: d2=8/d2=6 reveal countdowns clipped the title word,

### #336 reopened `[-]`→`[ ]` (human overrides the oracle with cross-emulator evidence)

The human played the original on **two emulators** and reports BLW1 does NOT show Kid floating in
the sky; it "fades from black and scrolls up from the ground." Kid does drop to the floor within
~1s in native (matches the prior "float then settle" presentation), so the dispute is about WHAT
IS VISIBLE during the camera ramp, not the camera/Kid-Y values. The 2026-06-23 closure proved only
camera/Kid-Y WRAM parity (`oracle-probe` of `Camera_Y_pos`/`Addr_GfxObject_Kid`) — it NEVER tested
the **palette fade-in (`Pal_FadeIn`) timing relative to the camera ramp**. Hypothesis: native
completes the fade-in earlier than the ROM, so the player SEES Kid mid-sky during frames the ROM
keeps black/dark while the camera scrolls down to ground. This is a NEW, untested dimension that
the WRAM probe did not cover, so the reopen is methodology-clean (not "trust the human over the
oracle" — the fade dimension is itself oracle-probeable via CRAM/palette dumps). P3: brief
visual-confusion, not game-breaking. DO NOT edit the `LEVEL_ONE_LOAD_INGAME_*_RAMP_Y` tables (the
camera/Kid-Y values are oracle-faithful per `c65df2500`); investigate the fade timing instead.

Fixed 2026-06-29: the reopened dimension was palette visibility, not WRAM state. Oracle CRAM probes
show `$FFFFF876` stays `$0000` through the black/load window, then the render-visible fade lags the
live Kid/camera ramp by three local frames: frame 974 applies `$0020`, frame 980 applies `$0080`
(`$0E62` blended to CRAM word `$0731`), and frame 984 applies `$00C0`. Native now exports
`level_entry_fade_progress_sub_73d0` for the title-card live handoff and the scene renderer applies
a final `PaletteFadeSub73D0` pass which quantises expanded MD RGB back to CRAM words and calls
`blend_palette_word_sub_14C0`. The dynamic route
`.cache/debug/issue336-cold-boot-live/scenario-card-start.json` stays CRC/checkpoint-clean for
frames 880..1041. Visual captures: frames 960/970 now have native/oracle AE=0; frame 974 means
0.004482/0.004403, frame 980 means 0.121883/0.123377, frame 984 means 0.187143/0.188333. Residual
AE after the fade starts is the pre-existing scene/HUD/tile difference, not fade timing. Verification:
focused core fade trace test, frame palette-fade tests, CLI scene-command test, `cargo check -q -p wildside-frame -p wildside-cli --tests`, route `verify-tas`, captures, and `mise run verify-slice-fast`.

### New rows opened

- **#357 (Lion one-stomp death as base Kid, P1 enemy).** Human stomped the Lion as **plain base
  Kid** and it died instantly "and/or definitely disappeared." ASM Lion HP = enemy_level+6 (min 6,
  Lion.asm:27/variables.asm:242); a `colid_kidabove` stomp only decrements `$44` by 1
  (`loc_3E32C`), dying solely at HP 0; instant death needs a signed-negative collision (special
  power, `loc_3E318 bmi`). So a base-Kid one-stomp kill is WRONG — likely a live-wiring gap (the
  stomp not delivered as a kidabove pending collision into `apply_pending_enemy_collisions`,
  combat.rs:8398, so the #315-wired HP-decrement never fires). The "disappeared" half overlaps
  #345. Probe: base-Kid stomp on a full-HP Lion should need ~6 hits with flashing between each.
  Cross-ref #186 (`[?]` Lion fidelity umbrella), #315, #345. NOT #239 (faithful ledge-fall cull).

- **#363 (Kid says "ouch" instead of "die" on death, P2 audio).** Human reports hearing the hurt

  DELIBERATELY KEPT on (a) helmet-loss contact and (b) survivable-hit-then-die. So "sometimes ouch
  on a full death" is, on its face, the preserved ROM exception (an ORIGINAL_QUIRK) UNLESS it is a
  clean single fatal contact with no helmet. The voice catalog is wired correct (VoiceOuch=0x61 /
  VoiceDie=0x60 / VoiceBummer=0x68, #340), and the ouch/die fix is NOT among the 9 candidates that
  failed validation per session-log. Action: capture the exact death cause, helmet state,
  hit-count, and audio transcript; if "ouch" fires on a clean single fatal CONTACT with no helmet,
  that is the regression. Cross-ref #308 (combat audit umbrella, currently `[b]`).
